problem:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 4 & -1 & 2 & -3 \\ -1 & 6 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & ={a}_{11}{C}_{11}+{a}_{12}{C}_{12}+{a}_{13}{C}_{13}+{a}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =(-3)\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13}+5\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =-3{C}_{11}+5{C}_{14} \\  & =(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ ∗ & -1 & 2 & -3 \\ ∗ & 6 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & ∗ \\ 4 & -1 & 2 & ∗ \\ -1 & 6 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)(-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & -3 \\ 6 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|+5(-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & -3 \\ 6 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|-5|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(0\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}|) \\  & -5(0\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|+3\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ -1 & 6\end{aligned}|) \\  & =-3\cdot (-3\cdot (0+18)+(-2)\cdot (0-12))-5\cdot (3\cdot (24-1)) \\  & =90-345 \\  & =-255\end{aligned}
$$
